title: Community Update
subtitle: EMERGENCY WILDLIFE ALERT
content:
Survivors across Nasdara Province are being warned following multiple sightings of large predatory creatures identified as raptors.

The creatures have reportedly been spotted roaming several major military installations, including FOBs, checkpoints and other strategic locations previously used by survivors for scavenging.

Witnesses describe the animals as exceptionally fast, aggressive and extremely dangerous. There are also indications that they may hunt in groups, making encounters particularly deadly.

Interestingly, reports suggest that these predators show little to no aggression towards the infected roaming in the same areas, raising further questions about their behaviour.

Survivors are strongly advised to avoid military installations whenever possible. Those who must enter should exercise extreme caution and come prepared.

Remember: the infected may no longer be the biggest threat waiting inside military compounds.

This has been Nasdara News Network. Stay alert. Stay alive.
author: Nasdara News Network

title: Community Update
subtitle: BREAKING REPORT
content:
Authorities and survivors across Nasdara Province are being urged to remain vigilant following a disturbing discovery made by local survivor Grooby Cutlet.

According to preliminary reports, Cutlet has uncovered what appears to be compelling evidence of an unusually large bear roaming the remote hills of the province. The findings reportedly include signs of a creature far larger than any known wildlife in the region.

While the evidence has yet to be independently verified, initial accounts have raised serious questions about what might be lurking beyond the settlements and military outposts.

Locals are being advised to avoid travelling alone through remote mountainous areas, particularly after dark. Hunters and scavengers are also being warned against approaching any suspicious tracks or remains.

Whether this is simply an unusually large animal or something far more concerning remains unknown.

One thing, however, is certain: the hills of Nasdara may no longer be as safe as we once thought.

This has been Nasdara News Network. Stay alert. Stay alive.
author: Nasdara News Network
